note: Paid delivery and shopping memberships: the published price, what members get, and the non-member fees a member doesn't pay, for pipeline/value.py. Every number was read on the company's own page (or a Wayback Machine copy of it, where the live page blocked automated reads), recorded in source_urls and dated in checked_on. null means the company doesn't publish that number (most say the fee 'varies' or is 'shown at checkout'); value.py then uses only what a receipt itself says it saved, and says there are not enough receipts to tell rather than guessing. No company publishes a sample receipt, so the receipt wording value.py looks for ('saved you $X', a waived fee line) is a pattern, not a quote.

memberships.notes: $9.99/month or $96/year from the Consumer Terms effective 2026-10-16. $0 delivery fee and reduced service fees on eligible restaurant orders over $12 (the DashPass page source and a help article). The non-member delivery fee 'varies by merchant', so only a receipt's own savings line counts.

$9.99/month or $96/year. $0 delivery fee and up to 10% off at participating stores on orders of $15 or more ($35 for grocery, from the page's own disclaimer text). 5% back in Uber One credits on eligible rides (the visible page text; one image says 6%, so the lower figure is used). Uber doesn't publish US non-member delivery fees.

memberships.not_counted: Its Peacock Premium is not counted.
memberships.notes: $9.99/month or $99/year. $0 delivery on grocery and retail orders of $10 or more (Costco $35, restaurants $25); service fees still apply. Non-members: 'delivery fees start at $3.99 for same-day orders over $35' (an instacart.com store page); other fees 'vary', so $3.99 per order is the cautious end and there is no published top end.

memberships.not_counted: Fuel savings and the included Paramount+ or Peacock aren't counted.
memberships.notes: Live pages show a robot check, so these were read from Wayback copies of the official pages (2026-10-08 /plus, 2026-10-09 benefits help, 2026-03-26 site help). $12.95/month or $98/year. Members don't pay the $7.95-$9.95 delivery-from-store fee; under the $35 order minimum they pay a $6.99 minimum-order fee instead, so the delivery fee still counts as saved. Shipping: members ship free with no minimum; non-members pay a $6.99 fee on orders under $35.

$9.99/month after the trial (no annual price published). $0 delivery fees on eligible orders, $12 or more on the partner version of the page. The Grubhub+ terms and Amazon's Prime page both say US Prime members get Grubhub+ at no cost once the accounts are linked. Non-member fees aren't published.

memberships.not_counted: Only shipping is counted: Prime Video, Music, Grubhub+ and fuel savings aren't.
memberships.notes: $14.99/month or $139/year (the Prime page). Without Prime, eligible orders over $35 ship free ('FREE delivery ... on orders shipped by Amazon over $35' on a signed-out product page; reports say Amazon tests $25 in some ZIP codes). Amazon no longer publishes the shipping charge under $35, so an order under $35 has no dollar estimate unless its email shows the shipping charge.
